title: K4 letters as skip counts through the sculpture's own text: moving window (rule A) and pointer walk (rule B) over 39 texts
k4_result: 16,060,464 settings, each giving one full 97-letter reading. Best 11 of 24 clue letters (rule A, K1-K3 plaintext with ? kept, read backwards, KRYPTOS numbering counted backwards, advance 8, start 404); 24 needed. By rule and mode: A ring 11, A line 8, B ring 9, B line 8. Mean per setting 1.12 of 24. Settings with 9+: 20, with 10+: 2, with 11+: 1. The readings are gibberish: the most English-looking of the 20 with 9+ clue letters scores -6.56 per quadgram (English is about -3.7, random letters -7.3); the six best by clue count score -6.56 to -6.84 with word coverage 0.08-0.26.
controls: 20 shuffled K4s, same search: best 9-11 of 24 (two at 9, seventeen at 10, one at 11). Settings with 9+: 17-50 each; with 10+: 0-8. K4 sits inside the controls on every count.
planted: 7/7 (rule A: 3 English messages through the tableau, ring and line, nearest and random choice, a = 31, 30, 0; rule B: 2 English messages walked through the tableau with a = 10, and 2 stretches of K1-K3 walked through K1-K3, ring and line). Each gave 24/24 at the planted text, numbering, advance and start, and the message was read back in full.
scope_limits: Covers only these exact letter strings: K1, K2 (carved and corrected), K3 plaintext; K1-K3 plaintext joined (carved, corrected, with ? kept, with K4 appended); K1-K3 ciphertext; the whole cipher panel (with and without ? cells); the tableau panel (as carved, body only, body with labels); the Morse text as transcribed in attack 58; the two panels joined either way; the two panels read by columns, back-and-forth and on diagonals (22 more readings). Each forwards and backwards, every start, ring and line. Count = place of the cipher letter in A-Z or the KRYPTOS alphabet, forwards or backwards, plus a fixed advance of 0..31 per letter (so numbering from 0 or 1 is included). One cipher letter = one count of at most 26 letters. NOT covered: any text not on the sculpture; counting words or lines instead of letters; counts built from two letters or larger than 26; a count that skips certain letters (spaces, X, ?); nulls or a transposition before or after; other numberings of the alphabet; a text with a transcription difference from the repository's. The clue pre-filter passes rule A and FLAGs rule B (a walk does not give K5 the same cipher letters for the same words); B was built anyway because the test is exact and takes two minutes.

negative.family: Cipher letter as a distance through the sculpture's text (skip-count / book-style reading)
negative.hypothesis: Each K4 letter is a count (its place in A-Z or KRYPTOS order) to step on through a text already on the sculpture, and the letter landed on is the plaintext; either from a window that moves a fixed amount per letter or as a running walk.
negative.scope: P_i = T[s + a*i +- d(C_i)] and P_i = T[q_i], q_i = q_(i-1) + a +- d(C_i); 39 texts (K1-K3 plaintexts and ciphertext, cipher panel, tableau panel, Morse, panels joined, panels by columns/back-and-forth/diagonals) x forwards/backwards x every start x a = 0..31 x A-Z/KRYPTOS numbering x both count directions, ring and line; 16,060,464 settings.
negative.outcome: Dead: best 11/24 clue letters where 24 are needed, readings gibberish (controls: 20 shuffled K4s give 9-11; planted 7/7 found at 24/24 and read back). Also: ordinary English can almost never be encoded this way on these texts (0 of 200 messages by either rule on the K1-K3 plaintext or the cipher panel; a walk dies after about 18 letters), so the method is not workable on prose however it is set.

follow_ups: Count words, not letters: each K4 letter (A=1..Z=26) says how many WORDS to move on through the K1-K3 plaintext, and the plaintext letter is the first (or last, or n-th) letter of that word. Word starts are far richer in the letters a message needs than a 26-letter window, so unlike letter counting this can actually encode English; it needs a fixed word division of K1-K3 (the X separators and the known words give one).

Coordinates instead of one count: K4 letters taken in pairs or with the position as (row, column) into the carved cipher panel or tableau (e.g. row from position i mod 28, column from the letter). Rule A with a = row length on the tableau is the only place where letter counting could encode English at all (20% of starts), and that is a plain tableau lookup, so the open variants are grid lookups with a non-linear row order.
